rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative may point to alif-lām-mīm as the letters composing the Qurʾān, to the sūra or Qurʾān after its utterance, or to the promised Book revealed now or in earlier scriptures.
rows.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى { الم } إن أول بالمؤلف من هذه الحروف أو فسر بالسورة أو القرآن فإنه لما تكلم به وتقضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāb is a verbal noun applied to its object for emphasis; alternatively it is a pattern meaning written object, applied to a composed discourse before writing because it is meant to be written. Its root means gathering.
rows.anchor: وهو مصدر سمي به المفعول للمبالغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is so clear and its proof so evident that sound reflection leaves no rational doubt that it is revelation at the level of inimitability; this does not mean nobody doubts it.
rows.anchor: لا أن أحدا لا يرتاب فيه، ألا ترى إلى قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 2:23 confirms that the challenge does not remove their initial doubt; it gives them a way to settle it by trying to compose one sūra and exhausting their effort, whose failure proves the Book beyond suspicion.
rows.anchor: فإنه ما أبعد عنهم الريب بل عرفهم الطريق المريح له، وهو أن يجتهدوا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative construal takes the negation as meaning that there is no doubt in the Book for the Godfearing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لا ريب فيه للمتقين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rayb originally denotes the anxiety and disturbance caused by something; doubt is called rayb because it unsettles the soul and removes tranquility, as in the cited saying and the phrase for time's calamities.
rows.anchor: والريب في الأصل مصدر رابني الشيء إذا حصل فيك الريبة، وهي قلق النفس واضطرابها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā means guidance, originally indication that leads people to the truth.
rows.anchor: يهديهم إلى الحق، والهدى في الأصل كالسرى والتقى ومعناه الدلالة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another definition is indication that reaches the sought goal, since guidance is contrasted with misguidance in 34:24 and one is called guided only on reaching the aim.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الدلالة الموصلة إلى البغية لأنه جعل مقابل الضلالة في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is singled out as guidance for the Godfearing because they follow and benefit from it, although its indication is available to every observer, Muslim or unbeliever; hence it is also called guidance for people.
rows.anchor: واختصاصه بالمتقين لأنهم المهتدون به والمنتفعون بنصه، وإن كانت دلالته عامة لكل ناظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, only people who refine their intellect, contemplate signs and miracles, and recognize prophecy benefit, just as good food benefits only someone already healthy; the Qurʾān heals believers but increases wrongdoers' loss.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه لا ينتفع بالتأمل فيه إلا من صقل العقل واستعمله في تدبر الآيات والنظر في المعجزات،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The presence of concise or ambiguous passages does not prevent the Qurʾān from being guidance, since it is accompanied by clarification that identifies their intended meaning.
rows.anchor: ولا يقدح ما فيه من المجمل والمتشابه في كونه هدى لما لم ينفك عن بيان يعين المراد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muttaqī is the active participle of guarding oneself; in religious usage it is one who protects oneself from harm in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والمتقي اسم فاعل من قولهم وقاه فاتقى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā has three ranks: avoiding eternal punishment by renouncing shirk (48:26); avoiding every sin of commission or omission, even minor sins according to some (7:96); and detaching from all that distracts from God and devoting oneself wholly to Him (3:102).
rows.anchor: وله ثلاث مراتب: الأولى: التوقي من العذاب المخلد بالتبري من الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī says the phrase is interpreted here according to all three ranks of taqwā.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر قوله: { هدى للمتقين } ههنا على الأوجه الثلاثة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing makes alif-lām-mīm the subject as a name for the Qurʾān, the sūra, or what is composed from these letters; dhālika is its predicate and al-kitāb describes the fully perfected composition.
rows.anchor: أن يكون { الم } مبتدأ على أنه اسم للقرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses make alif-lām-mīm the predicate of an omitted subject and dhālika a second predicate or apposition, with al-kitāb as its adjective; alternatively dhālika is the subject and al-kitāb its predicate or adjective.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون { الم } خبر مبتدأ محذوف وذلك خبرا ثانيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the common reading, rayb is accusative in construction with the categorical negative lā, which governs like inna and implies min.
rows.anchor: و { لا ريب } في المشهورة مبني لتضمنه معنى من منصوب المحل

rows.speaker: أبو الشعثاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Shaʿthāʾ reads rayb in the nominative, taking lā as lā of negation like laysa and fīhi as its predicate; this avoids restricting the negation to this book, unlike 37:47. The phrase may instead be an adjective with lil-muttaqīn as predicate.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي الشعثاء مرفوع بلا التي بمعنى ليس وفيه خبره ولم يقدم كما قدم في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā may be an accusative circumstantial phrase or have an omitted predicate as lā does; on the latter analysis, fīhi is the fronted predicate of the indefinite hudā, and the reciter pauses after lā rayba.
rows.anchor: وهدى نصب على الحال، أو الخبر محذوف كما في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes dhālika the subject and al-kitāb its predicate, meaning the complete book worthy of the name; or al-kitāb is an adjective and the following clause is the predicate of alif-lām-mīm.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون ذلك مبتدأ و { الكتب } خبره على معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī prefers treating the four clauses as a sequence without conjunctions, each confirming what precedes: the letters signal the challenge, the Book confirms its excellence, its freedom from doubt confirms perfection, and its guidance confirms truth.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يقال إنها جمل متناسقة تقرر اللاحقة منها السابقة ولذلك لم يدخل العاطف بينهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies a distinct rhetorical grace in each clause: ellipsis and allusion with explanation, the grandeur of definiteness, delayed adverbial wording avoiding a false implication, then ellipsis and an indefinite verbal noun for emphasis and magnificence.
rows.anchor: وفي كل واحدة منها نكتة ذات جزالة ففي الأولى الحذف والرمز إلى المقصود مع التعليل، وفي الثانية فخامة التعريف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The restriction of guidance to the pious is by outcome: those approaching taqwā are called pious, a concise wording that magnifies their standing.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الهدى بالمتقين باعتبار الغاية تسمية المشارف للتقوى متقيا إيجازا وتفخيما لشأنه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After listing the accountable groups and their traits, the discourse turns to direct address to startle and enliven the listener, stress worship's importance, magnify it, and ease its burden through the pleasure of being addressed.
rows.anchor: لما عدد فرق المكلفين وذكر خواصهم ومصارف أمورهم، أقبل عليهم بالخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yā normally calls someone distant but may address someone near as distant because of majesty, inattention or poor understanding, or to give the call greater emphasis and urgency.
rows.anchor: و (يا) حرف وضع لنداء البعيد، وقد ينادي به القريب تنزيلا له منزلة البعيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative and its particle form a meaningful clause because they stand in place of a verb. Ay bridges yā and a noun with al-, takes vocative status, and is clarified by the raised hādhā-like address; the inserted hā alerts and reinforces.
rows.anchor: وأي: جعل وصلة إلى نداء المعرف باللام، فإن إدخال «يا» عليه متعذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Definite plurals without a prior referent are general, as shown by the validity of exception and emphatic generalizers; the address covers people present at revelation and those yet to come under the Prophet's enduring law, except where evidence specifies otherwise.
rows.anchor: والجموع وأسماؤها المحلاة باللام للعموم حيث لا عهد، ويدل عليه صحة الاستثناء منها.

rows.speaker: علقمة والحسن
rows.claim: A report attributed to ʿAlqama and al-Ḥasan says every address beginning yā ayyuhā al-nās is Meccan and yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū is Medinan; Bayḍāwī says even if soundly raised to the Prophet, it does not restrict this command to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وما روي عن علقمة والحسن أن كل شيء نزل فيه { يا أيها الناس } فمكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addresses both unbelievers and believers: unbelievers must begin worship after the prerequisite knowledge and acknowledgment of the Creator, while believers must increase and persevere in worship; disbelief does not remove its obligation.
rows.anchor: فإن المأمور به هو القدر المشترك بين بدء العبادة، والزيادة فيها، والمواظبة عليها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God their Lord points to lordship as the reason worship is obligatory.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال: { ربكم } تنبيها على أن الموجب للعبادة هي الربوبية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhī is an attributive clause adding grandeur and explaining the reason for worship; if the addressees are specifically polytheists and rabb is taken broadly, it can instead distinguish the true Lord from their supposed lords.
rows.anchor: صفة جرت عليه تعالى للتعظيم والتعليل، ويحتمل التقييد والتوضيح إن خص الخطاب بالمشركين،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq means bringing something into existence proportioned and well-formed; its original sense is measuring, as in measuring and shaping a sandal to its dimensions.
rows.anchor: والخلق إيجاد الشيء على تقدير واستواء، وأصله التقدير يقال: خلق النعل إذا قدرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those before you includes everyone who precedes human beings essentially or in time; grammatically the phrase is accusative, coordinated with the object pronoun in khalaqakum.
rows.anchor: متناول كل ما يتقدم الإنسان بالذات أو بالزمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their creation is stated as something the audience acknowledges, as in 43:87, or can know by minimal reflection.
rows.anchor: والجملة أخرجت مخرج المقرر عندهم، إما لاعترافهم به كما قال الله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading repeats the relative pronoun in min qablikum, inserting it between the first relative pronoun and its clause for emphasis; Jarīr's repeated Taym in his line illustrates the construction.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { من قبلكم } على إقحام الموصول الثاني بين الأول وصلته تأكيدا، كما أقحم جرير في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿallakum tattaqūn may be circumstantial to the subject of worship: worship hoping to join the Godfearing, attain guidance and success, and merit God's presence.
rows.anchor: حال من الضمير في { اعبدوا } كأنه قال: اعبدوا ربكم راجين أن تنخرطوا في سلك المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā is the wayfarer's highest degree: turning from everything besides God toward Him. A worshipper should not be self-satisfied but should combine fear and hope.
rows.anchor: نبه به على أن التقوى منتهى درجات السالكين وهو التبري من كل شيء سوى الله تعالى إلى الله، وأن العابد ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is circumstantial to the objects of creation: God created the addressees and their predecessors in a state where taqwā is hoped for because its causes and incentives are abundant; the spoken addressees stand for all.
rows.anchor: أو من مفعول { خلقكم } والمعطوف عليه على معنى أنه خلقكم ومن قبلكم في صورة من يرجى منه التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes taqwa the purpose of creation, connecting the verse to 51:56, but Bayḍāwī calls it weak because this use lacks a linguistic parallel.
rows.anchor: وقيل تعليل للخلق أي خلقكم لكي تتقوا كما قال: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches that knowledge of God, His oneness, and His exclusive right to worship is reached by examining His works and reasoning from His acts.
rows.anchor: والآية تدل على أن الطريق إلى معرفة الله تعالى والعلم بوحدانيته واستحقاقه للعبادة، النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A servant earns no entitlement to reward through worship: worship is already owed in gratitude for prior blessings, like a worker paid before doing the work.
rows.anchor: فإنها لما وجبت عليه شكرا لما عدده عليه من النعم السابقة فهو كأجير أخذ الأجر قبل العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhī may be a second adjective, an accusative or nominative expression of praise, or a subject whose predicate is the prohibition fa-lā tajʿalū; jaʿala itself can mean become or begin intransitively, bring into being with one object, or render with two.
rows.anchor: صفة ثانية، أو مدح منصوب، أو مرفوع، أو مبتدأ خبره فلا تجعلوا وجعل من الأفعال العامة يجيء على ثلاثة أوجه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is made like a spread bed because some of it was raised above the enveloping water and balanced between hardness and softness, making it suitable for sitting and sleeping; this does not require a flat rather than spherical earth.
rows.anchor: جعل بعض جوانبها بارزا ظاهرا عن الماء، مع ما في طبعه من الإحاطة بها، وصيرها متوسطة بين الصلابة واللطافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven is a dome built over people, sheltering them.
rows.anchor: قبة مضروبة عليكم. والسماء اسم جنس يقع على الواحد والمتعدد كالدينار والدرهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samāʾ is a generic noun used for one or many, or is said to be the plural of samāʾah; bināʾ is a verbal noun applied to what is built, such as a house, dome, or tent, and the wedding phrase refers to setting up a new tent.
rows.anchor: والبناء مصدر، سمي به المبنى بيتا كان أو قبة أو خباء، ومنه بني على امرأته،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sending down of water is coordinated with God's making the earth a bed; fruits emerge through God's power and will, with water mixed into soil serving as means and material.
rows.anchor: عطف على (جعل)، وخروج الثمار بقدرة الله تعالى ومشيئته، ولكن جعل الماء الممزوج بالتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God either customarily imparts forms and qualities to mixed water and soil, or places active power in water and receptive power in earth; He could create things without causes or matter, but gradual creation renews lessons and steadies observers in awareness of His power.
rows.anchor: بأن أجرى عادته بإفاضة صورها وكيفياتها على المادة الممتزجة منهما، أو أودع في الماء قوة فاعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first min marks origin, whether sky means clouds (anything above is sky), the celestial sphere (rain passes from it to clouds then earth according to the apparent texts), or celestial causes lifting moisture to form rain clouds.
rows.anchor: و { من } الأولى للابتداء سواء أريد بالسماء السحاب فإن ما علاك سماء، أو الفلك فإن المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second min can be partitive, as 35:27 supports: not all water descends, not all fruit grows by rain, and not all sustenance consists of fruit; or it can explain the kind, with rizq meaning the provision received.
rows.anchor: و { من } الثانية للتبعيض بدليل قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamarāt can denote groups of individual fruits as a collective plural; the singular reading al-thamarah supports this explanation. Plurals may also exchange places, or the definite plural may fall outside the limit of paucity.
rows.anchor: وإنما ساغ الثمرات والموضع موضع الكثرة، لأنه أراد بالثمرات جماعة الثمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakum modifies rizq if it means the provision received; if rizq is a verbal noun, lakum is its object, meaning provision for you.
rows.anchor: و { لكم } صفة رزقا إن أريد به المرزوق ومفعوله إن أريد به المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-lā tajʿalū may coordinate a prohibition with worship, be subjunctive after an implied an, or depend on laʿalla so the sense is if you are mindful, do not make rivals; it may also be a prohibitive predicate of alladhī jaʿala.
rows.anchor: متعلق باعبدوا على أنه نهي معطوف عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal fāʾ links the prohibition to God's having singled people out for immense blessings and signs: the One who granted them should not be associated with.
rows.anchor: والفاء للسببية أدخلت عليه لتضمن المبتدأ معنى الشرط والمعنى: أن من خصكم بهذه النعم الجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nidd is an opposing equal or likeness; the word is reserved for a counterpart matching in essence, while a like in degree is called a musāwī. Jarīr's verse uses nidd for a rival.
rows.anchor:
قال جرير:
أتيما تجعلون إلي ندا
وما تيم لذي حسب نديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling idols rivals is sarcastic censure: polytheists need not claim equality with God in essence or attributes, but worshiping and naming them gods resembles believing they are self-existent and can repel harm or grant good.
rows.anchor: وتسمية ما يعبده المشركون من دون الله (أندادا)، وما زعموا أنها تساويه في ذاته وصفاته

rows.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل
rows.claim: The pre-Islamic monotheist Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl's verse contrasts worshiping one God with a thousand and declares that he abandoned al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال موحد الجاهلية زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل: أربا واحدا أم ألف رب أدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-antum taʿlamūn is circumstantial to the subject of fa-lā tajʿalū, with its object omitted: you are people of knowledge, reflection, and sound judgment.
rows.anchor: حال من ضمير فلا تجعلوا، ومفعول تعلمون مطروح، أي: وحالكم أنكم من أهل العلم والنظر وإصابة الرأي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the omitted object is that idols neither resemble God nor can do what He does, as 30:40 asks whether partners can do any such thing; the point is rebuke, not restricting the duty to the learned.
rows.anchor: أو منوي وهو أنها لا تماثله ولا تقدر على مثل ما يفعله كقوله سبحانه وتعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses command worship and forbid associating partners, then give their rationale: lordship grounds worship; God created people, their ancestors, and necessities of life, and these uniquely divine provisions witness His oneness.
rows.anchor: واعلم إن مضمون الآيتين هو الأمر بعبادة الله سبحانه وتعالى، والنهي عن الإشراك به تعالى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can also allude to human formation: body is earth, soul heaven, intellect water, and practical and theoretical virtues produced through intellect and senses are fruits of joined celestial active and earthly receptive powers.
rows.anchor: فمثل البدن بالأرض، والنفس بالسماء، والعقل بالماء، وما أفاض عليه من الفضائل العملية والنظرية

words: قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels admit their limitation, show their question was inquiry rather than objection, recognize the revealed human excellence and wisdom of creation, thank God for teaching them, and defer all knowledge to Him.
rows.anchor: اعتراف بالعجز والقصور، وإشعار بأن سؤالهم كان استفسارا ولم يكن اعتراضا، وأنه قد بان لهم ما خفي عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥān is a verbal noun like ghufrān, almost always used in an accusative construct with its verb understood, as in maʿādh Allāh; a poet exceptionally uses it as a predicate noun for glorification.
rows.anchor: وسبحان: مصدر كغفران ولا يكاد يستعمل إلا مضافا منصوبا بإضمار فعله، كمعاذ الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning with subḥān apologizes for inquiry and ignorance; it likewise opens repentance in Moses' words in 7:143 and Jonah's in 21:87.
rows.anchor: وتصدير الكلام به اعتذار عن الاستفسار والجهل بحقيقة الحال، ولذلك جعل مفتاح التوبة فقال موسى عليه السلام:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAlīm means that nothing is hidden from God; al-Ḥakīm means He perfectly orders His creations and acts only with profound wisdom.
rows.anchor: العليم } الذي لا يخفي عليه خافية. { الحكيم } المحكم لمبدعاته الذي لا يفعل إلا ما فيه حكمة بالغة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anta may be a separating pronoun or emphasis on the attached second-person pronoun, a use allowed to a dependent element but not as a standalone object; alternatively it is the subject of a clause predicated of inna.
rows.anchor: وأنت فصل، وقيل: تأكيد للكاف كما في قولك: مررت بك أنت، وإن لم يجز: مررت بأنت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anbiʾhum means inform them; readings turn the hamza into yāʾ or omit it, with kasra on the hāʾ in both forms.
rows.anchor: أي: أعلمهم، وقرىء بقلب الهمزة ياء وحذفها بكسر الهاء فيهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Adam informs the angels, God's question restates 2:30 in fuller form as evidence: He knows hidden matters of heaven and earth and their outward and inward conditions, including what they did not know.
rows.anchor: استحضار لقوله تعالى: إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون [البقرة: 30] لكنه جاء به على وجه أبسط ليكون كالحجة عليه،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says what the angels displayed was their question, Will You place there someone who causes corruption?
rows.anchor: وقيل: { ما تبدون } قولهم: أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On that explanation, what they concealed was their belief that they deserved the vicegerency more and that God would create no better being than them.
rows.anchor: وما { تكتمون } استبطانهم أنهم أحقاء بالخلافة، وأنه تعالى لا يخلق خلقا أفضل منهم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second explanation takes what they displayed as obedience and what Iblīs concealed from them as his disobedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما أظهروا من الطاعة، وأسر إبليس منهم من المعصية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza expresses denial; entering on a negative particle turns the question into an affirmative confirmation.
rows.anchor: والهمزة للإنكار دخلت حرف الجحد فأفادت الإثبات والتقرير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage establishes human nobility and the superiority of knowledge to worship; knowledge is a condition and central qualification for vicegerency, and Adam's greater knowledge makes him superior to the angels, as 39:9 states.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذه الآيات تدل على شرف الإنسان، ومزية العلم وفضله على العبادة، وأنه شرط في الخلافة بل العمدة فيها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching may be attributed to God, though al-Muʿallim is not used as His title because it denotes someone who practices teaching professionally.
rows.anchor: وأن التعليم يصح إسناده إلى الله تعالى، وإن لم يصح إطلاق المعلم عليه لاختصاصه بمن يحترف به،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports divinely instituted languages: teaching the names means conveying words with their meanings, which presupposes prior designation; since no one before Adam could have designated them, God did so.
rows.anchor: وأن اللغات توقيفية، فإن الأسماء تدل على الألفاظ بخصوص أو عموم، وتعليمها ظاهر في إلقائها على المتعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is a concept beyond knowledge; otherwise the pairing All-Knowing, All-Wise would be redundant.
rows.anchor: وأن مفهوم الحكمة زائد على مفهوم العلم وإلا لتكرر قوله: { إنك أنت العليم الحكيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' knowledge and perfections can increase, contrary to philosophers who deny increase for the highest angelic rank and interpret 37:164 as fixing each one's station.
rows.anchor: وأن علوم الملائكة وكمالاتهم تقبل الزيادة، والحكماء منعوا ذلك في الطبقة العليا منهم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows things before they come into existence.
rows.anchor: وأنه تعالى يعلم الأشياء قبل حدوثها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a forceful assertion that rebukes and expresses astonishment.
rows.anchor: تقرير مع توبيخ وتعجيب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birr means breadth in doing good, from barr, an open expanse; it includes every good and comprises devotion to God, care for relatives, and kindness to strangers.
rows.anchor: والبر: التوسع في الخير، من البر وهو الفضاء الواسع يتناول كل خير، ولذلك قيل ثلاثة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting yourselves means leaving yourselves out of the good you urge on others, as though you were forgotten.
rows.anchor: وتنسون أنفسكم } وتتركونها من البر كالمنسيات،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about learned rabbis in Medina who privately urged people they advised to follow Muḥammad but did not follow him themselves.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنها نزلت في أحبار المدينة، كانوا يأمرون سرا من نصحوه باتباع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا يتبعونه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says they commanded almsgiving but did not give charity themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يأمرون بالصدقة ولا يتصدقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that they recite Scripture censures them, like the phrase while you know; the Torah warns against stubbornness, abandoning good, and making practice contradict speech.
rows.anchor: تبكيت كقوله: { وأنتم تعلمون } أي تتلون التوراة، وفيها الوعيد على العناد وترك البر ومخالفة القول العمل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may ask whether they perceive the ugliness of their conduct and so desist, or whether they lack the intellect to stop what they know has a bad outcome. ʿAql originally means restraint.
rows.anchor: قبح صنيعكم فيصدكم عنه، أو أفلا عقل لكم يمنعكم عما تعلمون وخامة عاقبته. والعقل في الأصل الحبس،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns the preacher who does not practice his own counsel, urging self-purification so he can improve others; it does not forbid a sinner to preach, since failing one duty does not cancel another.
rows.anchor: والآية ناعية على من يعظ غيره ولا يتعظ بنفسه سوء صنيعه وخبث نفسه، وأن فعله فعل الجاهل بالشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge of greatest wrongdoing is general: it applies to anyone who destroys a mosque or works to disable a place designated for prayer.
rows.anchor: عام لكل من خرب مسجدا، أو سعى في تعطيل مكان مرشح للصلاة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion of revelation is the Romans' invasion of Jerusalem, destruction of the sanctuary, and killing of its people.
rows.anchor: وإن نزل في الروم لما غزوا بيت المقدس وخربوه وقتلوا أهله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it concerns the polytheists preventing the Prophet from entering the Sacred Mosque in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: أو في المشركين لما منعوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يدخل المسجد الحرام عام الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause an yudhkara fīhā ismuhu is the second object of the verb manaʿa.
rows.anchor: ثاني مفعولي منع { وسعى فى خرابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking the mosques' ruin means demolishing them or disabling them from use.
rows.anchor: وسعى فى خرابها } بالهدم، أو التعطيل

words: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ إِلَّا خَآئِفِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the wrongdoers ought only to enter with fear and reverence, since they destroyed the mosque.
rows.anchor: ما كان ينبغي لهم أن يدخلوها إلا بخشية وخشوع فضلا عن أن يجترئوا على تخريبها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says their only rightful entry would be in fear that believers might strike them, let alone their preventing believers from entering.
rows.anchor: أو ما كان الحق أن يدخلوها إلا خائفين من المؤمنين أن يبطشوا بهم، فضلا عن أن يمنعوهم منها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third construal refers to God's knowledge and decree, promising believers victory and recovery of the mosques; Bayḍāwī says that promise was fulfilled.
rows.anchor: أو ما كان لهم في علم الله وقضائه، فيكون وعدا للمؤمنين بالنصرة واستخلاص المساجد منهم وقد نجز وعده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the verse forbid allowing them into the mosque. The jurists differ: Abū Ḥanīfa permits entry, Mālik forbids it, and al-Shāfiʿī distinguishes the Sacred Mosque from other mosques.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه النهي عن تمكينهم من الدخول في المسجد، واختلف الأئمة فيه فجوز أبو حنيفة ومنع مالك، وفرق الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly disgrace may be killing and captivity, or the imposition of the poll tax.
rows.anchor: قتل وسبي، أو ذلك بضرب الجزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their great punishment in the afterlife is for their unbelief and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: عذاب عظيم } بكفرهم وظلمهم.
